chapter: New Orleans and Havana with Benbow
title: Havana, sensation drummer Little Rastus, and learning Spanish
summary: The show went to Havana, following another act; Moore describes a showy drummer sliding on his stomach, his $40 weekly pay, and a comic attempt at Spanish with a girl.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So we went to, after you left New Orleans, we went to Havana Cuba. And we stayed down there about four months. We was following Gonzalo White. I think that was his name. And that's when I, first, first time I remember seeing rasters, little rasters, little drummer rasters. Great sensation drummer. I was kind of fly there during that time of set, but I wasn't fly as he was. He used to make a running spin slide on his stomach and hit the bass drum and cymbal right on the beat. The band would be playing. Any time he would be playing, he'd make a running thing the band was still playing and turn around and face the drum with two sticks and made a slide on his stomach. And on the end of the, on the end of the number, he would slide there just in time to hit that cymbal and bass drum. Vroom! He's a great little dancer too. He's a sensation drummer. He's one of the sensation drummers. I was getting $40 a week with Benbo. So when they come back, we played, we hit, we come out of the way by Key West Florida. We started playing all through Florida. How'd you like Cuba? Wonderful. Only thing about it, I learned to speak a few words in Spanish. I learned how to speak for, I asked for rice, yellow rice, or rice, yellow rice. Coffee with milk in it, coffee lector, as we have pronounced it. And beef, beef steak and potatoes, call it beef steak and papatritas. And when I see a good looking chick, I look at her, hey baby. She could understand what I was talking about, see. So I find out the way, what I would have said to somebody to talk and say, don't be talking about, hey baby. See, just take your hand and do this. She knew what you mean.
Like you're knocking on the door.
Yeah, she knew what you mean. So I picked up on one of them all like that. I said, hey baby.
She said, man, don't say no, hey baby, do this.

So I looked at the girl, got her eye, and I did this. And she come over to me. I said, you want to have a drink with me? She said, man, they don't know nobody speaking no, no. Speak Spanish. I said, all right, you be my intent, you speak funny. Tell her what I want to have a drink with. So I mean, let me come on back down, bed off in Florida.
